title: Single Use Technology Expert
fitWhy: Asks for 3+ years in process development or MS&T plus technical selling and project management, with revenue targets for the single-use portfolio. Your PranaX cleanroom build-out, tech transfer and scale-up match the technical half; the Rice MBA covers the commercial half.
gaps: No formal technical-sales title yet. Frame PranaX equipment procurement and vendor qualification as the customer-side view of what Sartorius sells.
posting: Remote role in Bioprocess Solutions. Own revenue growth for the single-use portfolio with sales and field application specialists; protect run-rate business; work with MSAT/PD scientists to design and implement single-use assemblies; project-manage SUT projects across Product Management, Quality and Engineering. Wants BS in life science/engineering (MS a plus), 3+ yrs PD or process/manufacturing support, ~1 yr technical selling, project management, knowledge of ISO, USP, extractables/leachables.
tailoring: Lead your summary with 'MSAT scientist and Rice MBA' so both halves show in the first line.
Under PranaX, add a bullet on equipment and consumables selection and vendor management, if accurate, with scale (number of vendors, budget).
If you used single-use bioreactors, bags or tubing assemblies, name them explicitly; the posting screens for single-use experience.
Mention any extractables/leachables or USP <665>/<661> work, even if minor.

draft.coverLetter:
Dear Sartorius Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Single Use Technology Expert role in Bioprocess Solutions. For the past two years I have been on the customer side of the conversations this role leads. As the first employee at PranaX, I built and ran an ISO-certified cleanroom for GMP exosome manufacturing, and I selected, procured and qualified the equipment that process runs on.

That work covered the full path from process development to clinical manufacturing: technology transfer, scale-up, IQ/OQ/PQ, aseptic operations, batch records, QC, and regulatory alignment. I know what an MSAT or PD scientist needs to see before committing to a new technology, because I had to justify those choices to quality and to leadership myself.

I recently completed my MBA at Rice University, and I am moving deliberately toward roles that combine technical depth with commercial responsibility. This position does that directly. It means owning growth for the single-use portfolio alongside sales and field application specialists, and running projects that bring Product Management, Quality and Engineering together around a customer's process.

Before PranaX, I spent three years as a research scientist in the Kalluri Laboratory at MD Anderson, engineering extracellular vesicles for vaccine delivery and preparing MSC-derived EVs for GLP studies. That work contributed to six peer-reviewed publications. Today I lead operational build-out for the CPRIT Texas EVCore at MD Anderson, where I scope custom projects with investigators and clients and deliver results under SOP-controlled workflows.

I would welcome the chance to discuss how my manufacturing background and business training could help Sartorius grow single-use adoption with process development and MS&T teams.

Sincerely,
Arya Arian
